verdict.rationale: Apify's first-party webhooks let you configure the platform to perform an action automatically when a system event occurs. Examples include an HTTP request to another service, or starting another Actor when a run finishes or fails. That is event-triggered automation configured on the product itself. Schedules (apify-docs-6) are time-based, not event-based, so they were not credited. Missing for 10: a documented catalog of event types, conditional or filtering rule logic beyond event-to-action binding, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Webhooks provide an easy and reliable way to configure the Apify platform to carry out an action (e.g. a HTTP request to another service) when a certain system event
you can use webhooks to start another Actor when an Actor run finishes or fails.
